Hi Alice — thanks for the clear list. Quick written recap and proposed next steps below. I've attached a short SOC2 excerpt and an encryption-options workbook for your review.

Recap / answers (high level):
- In-transit: TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3 supported for all hosted/private deployments. Mutual TLS is supported for Private (VPC) and Dedicated options; Hosted API supports mTLS for partner/private endpoints on request.
- At-rest: We support platform-managed keys by default and Customer-Managed Keys (CMEK/BYOK) for Dedicated and Private deployments. Supported providers: AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault.
- HSM/EKM: For enterprise Private deployments we can integrate with customer HSMs or external key managers (EKM). Keys are not exportable from managed HSMs; for BYOK we provide clear guidance on key wrapping and lifecycle.
- Logging & retention: Logs can be configured per-route. We offer redaction for PII in request/response logs, and retention policies (30/90/365 days) with the ability to shorten or disable retention for specific routes.
- Data residency: Private deployments can be pinned to region or on-prem. For hosted accounts we offer region routing and EU-pin options for enterprise contracts.

Next steps I propose:
1) Rishi to outline technical implementation details for CMEK/BYOK and HSM integration (see note below).
2) Dev to schedule a 1-hour tech deep-dive with your security/infra team to walk through the KMS onboarding checklist and timing.
3) I will share the encryption whitepaper + SOC2 excerpt (attached) and a proposed timeline for enabling CMEK on Dedicated.

Hi Alice / Marissa — following up with more technical detail on KMS/CMEK options and constraints so PayWise's infra team can evaluate. High-level points then specifics:

High-level:
- We support CMEK (BYOK) for Dedicated and Private. Hosted customers can enable CMEK under enterprise contract with an EKM integration.
- We integrate with AWS KMS, GCP Cloud KMS, and Azure Key Vault. For HSM-level protection we support Cloud HSM partners (AWS CloudHSM, Google Cloud HSM) or on-prem HSMs via EKM.

Details:
1) Key lifecycle & rotation:
   - Keys are referenced by key ARN/ID; Redwood never stores plaintext keys.
   - We support automatic rotation triggers and customer-initiated rotation. Rolling key rotation is supported; you must ensure existing wrapped keys are available for re-wrapping token caches.
2) Key usage model:
   - Envelope encryption: Data encryption keys (DEKs) are generated per volume/request and wrapped with your KMS key. This avoids frequent KMS QPS for per-token ops.
   - Cache/EVP: For model KV caches we store only encrypted DEKs; plaintext DEKs exist in-memory transiently during operations (protected by process isolation and memory protections).
3) Exportability / HSM:
   - Managed HSMs: not exportable. BYOK where customer generates key material off-box and imports wrapped key is supported for some providers; details depend on provider and contract.
4) Mutual TLS / In-transit:
   - TLS 1.3 default; mTLS supported on Private/Dedicated endpoints. Certificate management options include customer-supplied certs or Redwood-managed cert rotation.
5) Logging & PII controls:
   - Request/response logs can be filtered to redact fields, redact full request bodies, or retain only metadata.
   - Audit logs (who/when) are available to you; PII redaction is configurable for request content and can be enforced at route level.
6) Operational prerequisites:
   - For CMEK onboarding we need: key policy that allows Redwood service principal to encrypt/decrypt (or EKM connector), an initial key rotation window, and a test key for end-to-end validation.

Estimated timeline (Dedicated/Private):
- Kickoff & key policy alignment: 1 week
- Integration and validation: 2-3 weeks
- Production enablement & runbook handover: 1 week

I'll be available on the deep-dive; happy to share a KMS onboarding checklist and example IAM policies.

—Rishi
